selected.how: Assumes the global minimum is the smallest even value; fails when the global minimum is odd but a larger even value exists.

selected.where: Uses arr.index(min_value) to find the index of the smallest even value.
selected.how: index() returns the first occurrence of the value; if the global minimum is even but appears later than another even value, the wrong index is returned.
selected.what: Input [2, 0, 2] returns [0, 1] correctly, but if logic relied on index of a non-first duplicate, it would fail; here it works for 0, but the mechanism is fragile if min_value wasn't unique.

selected.where: Calls min(arr) on the entire array without filtering for even values first.
selected.how: min() is applied to an unfiltered collection; if the array contains only odd numbers, min() returns an odd number, leading to incorrect logic flow.
selected.what: Input [1, 3, 5] returns [1, 0] (odd) instead of [] (no even values).
